title: Bitcoin hits a two-year low

lines: Bitcoin has now dropped more than 50% from its record high.
This weekend it fell to its lowest price in two years.
Bitcoin sank to about $55,000 on Saturday before rebounding toward $60,000.
It's down more than 20% in November — one of its weakest Novembers in years. (Crypto Briefing, Nov. 20-21)
The trigger isn't really crypto — it's AI.
The same valuation fear that pulled the Nasdaq negative for 2026 is spilling out of tech stocks and into bitcoin.
Spot bitcoin now sits in brokerage accounts, some U.S. 401(k)s and Canadian crypto ETFs. Fund outflows are mounting, and the Fear & Greed Index reads 11 — 'extreme fear.'
Weekends like this run on leverage and forced selling — not on people suddenly changing their minds about bitcoin.
Does a 50% drop make bitcoin look risky to you — or cheap?

caption:
Bitcoin just hit its lowest price in two years — and it's no longer only a crypto story.

It fell to about $55,000 on Saturday before rebounding toward $60,000, leaving it down more than 20% this month and over 50% below the $126,000 record it set on Oct. 6, 2025 (Crypto Briefing, Nov. 20-21).

Why it lands on you even if you never bought any: spot bitcoin now sits in brokerage accounts, some 401(k)s and Canadian crypto ETFs — and the same AI-valuation fear that pulled the Nasdaq negative for 2026 is now spilling into crypto. Fund outflows are mounting and the Fear & Greed Index reads 11, 'extreme fear.'

My take: weekends like this run on leverage and forced selling, not on people changing their minds.

Does a 50% drop make bitcoin look risky to you, or cheap?
